modern: No longer wander aimlessly; for you will not read your own memoirs, nor the deeds of the ancient Romans and Hellenes, and the selections from books which you were saving for your old age. Hurry, then, to the end which you have before you, and, throwing away idle hopes, come to your own aid, if you care at all for yourself, while it is in your power.
original: No longer wander at hazard; for neither wilt thou read thy own memoirs, nor the acts of the ancient Romans and Hellenes, and the selections from books which thou wast reserving for thy old age. Hasten then to the end which thou hast before thee, and, throwing away idle hopes, come to thy own aid, if thou carest at all for thyself, while it is in thy power.
